Patient: Marcus Oyelaran  
Service: Emergency department visit, level 5 (CPT 99285), CT angiogram chest  
Date of Service: October 11, 2026  

This letter constitutes a formal first-level appeal of the adverse benefit determination dated October 23, 2026, denying coverage for the emergency department visit and CT angiogram chest performed on October 11, 2026, at St. Agnes Regional Medical Center. The denial was based on the reason: “Services were provided by a facility that does not participate in the Blue Meridian network. Your plan does not cover non-emergency services from out-of-network providers.” (Denial Code: NN-12). This denial is incorrect and must be reversed, as the services rendered were emergency in nature and therefore fully covered under the plan’s terms.

Under Article 3 of the Blue Meridian Summary Plan Description, emergency services are covered in-network and out-of-network without prior authorization. Emergency services provided by an out-of-network facility are to be covered at the in-network cost-sharing level. An emergency medical condition is defined as a condition manifesting itself by acute symptoms of sufficient severity, including severe pain, such that a prudent layperson, possessing average knowledge of health and medicine, could reasonably expect the absence of immediate medical attention to result in serious jeopardy to health. The patient presented with sudden sharp chest pain radiating to the back and shortness of breath beginning at 01:30 while driving on I-75, as documented in the St. Agnes Regional Medical Center Emergency Department Record dated October 11, 2026. Vital signs showed hypertension (BP 178/104), tachycardia (HR 118), and low oxygen saturation (SpO2 93%), prompting ESI level 2 triage. The final diagnosis was acute chest pain and hypertensive urgency. These findings meet the prudent layperson standard for an emergency medical condition, triggering coverage under Article 3 regardless of network status.

Furthermore, the patient had no ability to select an in-network facility, as he was transported by emergency medical services to the nearest emergency department due to the acuity of his symptoms. The medical record explicitly states: “Patient brought by EMS; St. Agnes was the nearest emergency department (4.1 miles).” The patient affirms: “I had no way to choose an in-network ER.” Because the patient was incapacitated by severe symptoms and required immediate transport, imposing network restrictions violates the intent of Article 3 and unfairly penalizes the patient for accessing the only viable option for timely emergency care.

Article 4 of the plan, which restricts coverage for non-emergency out-of-network services without a referral, does not apply here. That provision expressly limits its scope to non-emergency services. As established, the services rendered were emergency in nature, supported by the patient’s symptomatology, ESI level 2 triage, and clinical diagnosis. Applying Article 4 to this emergency encounter misinterprets the plan’s language and contradicts the explicit emergency services guarantee in Article 3.

Additionally, the patient is protected from balance billing for emergency services under Article 9 of the plan, which incorporates federal requirements including the No Surprises Act. This federal law prohibits surprise billing for emergency care regardless of network status, reinforcing that the plan must cover these services at in-network levels.

As an employer-sponsored plan governed by ERISA, Blue Meridian is obligated to provide a full and fair review of this appeal in accordance with ERISA Section 503 and 29 CFR 2560.503-1, as stated in Article 8 of the plan. I respectfully request that the denial be overturned, that the claim be processed and paid at the in-network benefit level, and that I be provided with a peer-to-peer review opportunity and a complete copy of the claim file and all criteria used in the initial determination.

Enclosures:  
- Copy of the denial letter citing denial reason and code NN-12  
- Itemized bill from St. Agnes Regional Medical Center for the ED visit and CT angiogram  

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and advise of the expected timeline for resolution, as post-service appeals must be decided within 60 days per Article 8. Thank you for your prompt attention to this urgent matter.
